Subject: Pilot requirements - regional routing + no-fallback

Hi Logan,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Acme Health is ready to run a 6-week pilot focused on PHI ingestion from our patient intake flows. Before we spin up the pilot we need two hard constraints from Redwood:

1) All inference traffic must be routed to the US-only deployment and never fail over to other regions.
2) For this pilot we need a guarantee that the inference runtime will not auto-fallback to any alternate model or variant (no-fallback). Any fallback behavior needs to be explicitly approved by our security team.

These are non-negotiable for the initial pilot due to our internal compliance and audit controls.

I've attached our completed security questionnaire and the signed MRA. Can you confirm whether Redwood can support the above constraints and what the operational impact will be (SLOs, runbooks, expected latency headroom)? We also need an estimate for any add-on fees for dedicated routing / model pinning.

Best,
Julia

Thanks for the ping, Logan.

Short answer: yes, we can meet these constraints but with operational caveats and recommended mitigations. Details below.

What we can offer today:
- Private (VPC) deployment or Dedicated capacity pinned to US regions with model version pinning. That combination prevents automatic cross-region routing and keeps the model binary within the customer's region.
- No-fallback behavior: we can configure the routing policy to disallow automatic fallback to alternate model variants. That will force requests to either succeed on the pinned variant or surface an error.

Operational tradeoffs & risks:
- Availability: with no automatic fallback, incidents affecting the pinned model's nodes (hardware, driver bugs, kernel regressions) will cause request errors until manual remediation or switchover. We recommend a short manual failover play rather than silent fallback to preserve auditability.
- Latency/throughput: Dedicated pools sized for peak will cover expected latency; however, we need explicit sizing numbers from Acme (qps, seq length). Without KV cache sharing to other regions, token cost and cold-starts can increase.

Required steps to enable pilot:
1) Legal/finance sign the amended MRA (we have the signed copy, thx).
2) Provision Dedicated US pool with model pinned (PRIORITY).
3) Ops to produce a no-fallback runbook (attached stub: ops_runbook_no_fallback.md).
4) Security to review questionnaire and confirm controls (network ACLs, KMS, audit logs).

Timeline: if we get final qps/latency targets today, ops can provision and validate a small pilot in 5 business days. Full-scale provision ~2-3 weeks depending on capacity lead time.

Cost: There will be an incremental monthly fee for dedicated reservation + a one-time provisioning/validation fee. I'll coordinate with finance for exact numbers.

Julia — two asks for you so we can proceed: (1) a short qps/traffic profile for the pilot (expected concurrent requests, avg token length), and (2) confirmation who from Acme security will be the sign-off contact.

-Kim

Appreciate the thread. I'm comfortable approving a controlled exception with conditions.

Decision summary (approved):
- Approval: Temporary "no-fallback" + US-only routing for Acme Health pilot (6 weeks) under Dedicated US capacity.
- Conditions:
  * Ops must implement the attached runbook and perform a canary validation before start.
  * Security lead at Acme must be named and perform a checklist-based sign-off (network/KMS/audit).
  * We will not enable auto-billing overages; finance to set a committed cap and apply a pilot discount.
  * Exception window: 90 days from go-live; extension requires product+security exec review.

Priyom — please coordinate capacity provisioning and the canary validation (size for 5 qps initially, validate for 48 hours). Share the runbook with Acme's security contact and ops.

Logan — go ahead and reply to Julia with the approved constraints, expected timeline (ops 5 business days for canary), and ask for the qps profile & security contact. I'll loop in legal if there are MRA ammendments needed.

-Markus
